name: SyntAct
full_title: SyntAct: A Synthesized Database of Basic Emotions
status_note: Implemented with 6 classes (angry/boredom/fear/happy/neutral/sad). Synthetic speech (MBROLA + rules); labels are the emotion specified at synthesis. Of 6,001 wav files, the neutral side of 30 sad/neutral pairs with identical md5 is excluded, leaving 5,971. The maintainer's assessment: "quite poor synthetic data; unsure whether to use it in experiments" (2026-10-20).
license_note: Zenodo record 6573016: CC BY 4.0 (the API and the web page agree). The CC-BY-NC-4.0 in the paper text is separate from the data license. SuperKogito's list says CC BY-SA 4.0, a secondary source that disagrees with the primary one (Zenodo), so it is not adopted.
release_version: Zenodo version 1.0 (published 2022-05-23). syntact_cat.zip 986,508,556 B, md5 e5e3ba24f70edc3193a007047fec5870
labels_discrete_note: Labels are the emotion specified at synthesis (the `desired` table). 30 pairs, sad number n and neutral number n+1, are byte-identical (all in train); the loudness is close to sad, so the neutral side appears wrong and the recipe excludes it. md5 finds no similar errors for other emotions.
label_basis_note: MBROLA diphone synthesis with rule-based prosody manipulation for 3 emotions and neutral. Labels are the synthesis target emotion. When the rules were set, a forced-choice listening experiment with 20 participants gave a mean accuracy of 0.5 (not a per-clip selection).
lexical_confound_note: German news sentences (Leipzig corpus) assigned in file order, so the content is independent of the emotion.
notes: Burkhardt, Eyben, Schuller (LREC 2022 DCLRL workshop). Synthetic data (not human speech): MBROLA diphone synthesis with emotion-like prosody applied by Emofilt rules. Sentences are distinct sentences from the Leipzig University German news corpus; transcripts are not in the release. The release has 6,001 wav files (the paper says 6,000; reads as a one-off from the generation script's stop condition, but that is a guess). 16 kHz mono 16-bit, 0.819-30.506 s, 11.1437 h in total, 6 voices. The official split is by voice: train de1-de4 (3,620), test de6 and de7 (2,381). 30 pairs, sad n and neutral n+1, are fully byte-identical (de1 9, de2 7, de4 14, all in train). Cause unverified (hypothesis: the generation script reuses a temporary file and does not check for failure). The paper's listening test (20 people, forced choice) gives neutral .6, happiness .35, sadness .5, anger .55 (mean .5): hard for people to tell apart. Voice genders disagree between sources (paper and `db.yaml` vs the GitHub script), so none are given. The Zenodo description says "three basic emotions", but the paper and release have 5 + neutral, 6 classes. The maintainer's assessment: quite poor synthetic data; unsure whether to use it in experiments (2026-10-20).

name: Talrómur 3
status_note: Implemented with 6 styles (neutral / happy / sad / angry / surprise / helpful), all used as classes; uses 20,376 of the 21,516 FLAC (the 1,140 addendum and addendum_style2 recordings of numbers and letters are left out by the maintainer's decision; their existence is recorded). helpful is a speaking style rather than an emotion and is used like the others (the aim is a general paralinguistic model). The counts in the page description, Size field and README (21,528 / 21,518 / 21,526) disagree with each other and with the files (21,516).
license_note: CLARIN-IS page (re-read 2026-10-26): 'This item is Publicly Available and licensed under Creative Commons - Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)'. The page text and the README also call it a public domain corpus; the stricter CC BY 4.0 is adopted (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-25).
labels_discrete_note: neutral, happy, sad, angry, surprised, helpful (helpful is a speaking style, not an emotion)
label_basis_note: Label = the style the voice talent was instructed to read in (neutral, happy, sad, angry, surprised, helpful), with an instructed intensity 1-5 for the non-neutral styles. The README describes no rating of the recordings.
lexical_confound_note: The same 340 sentences are read in all six styles by every speaker (counted from index.tsv), so the words carry no label information, although the README says the prompt list contains prompts matching each emotion. The sentences come from interview and speech transcripts and message boards.
notes: Ornolfsson, Sigurgeirsson, Nikulasdottir and Schnell (Reykjavik University and Grammatek, Icelandic Language Technology Programme, recorded in 2024); CLARIN-IS v1.0 (2025-08-25), recordings.zip 6.34 GB, vad.zip (Silero VAD) and the README. Icelandic. 10 voice talents (5 female, 5 male) chosen from 97 applicants by a two-stage review, reading 340 sentences in 6 styles (neutral, happy, sad, angry, surprised, helpful) with an instructed intensity 1-5, plus 57 short items (numbers 0-20 and letters) in 2 styles (addendum in isolation, addendum_style2 in enumeration). Sentences come from speech and interview transcripts and message boards. Speakers M03 and M04 skipped two sentences (ids 262 and 325) in the non-neutral styles (338 each). 21,516 FLAC (48 kHz 24-bit mono), 24.22 h in total. The folder of speaker M02 has a typo (suprised) for one style. Intensity values are randomised per participant but repeated across styles. The item also holds Silero VAD values (vad.zip) and MFA phoneme alignments (alignment.zip, alignment_json.zip), which the recipe does not download; the README advises caution with the alignments. No byte-level duplicate check was made.

name: Telugu Emotion Speech (Kaggle jettysowmith)
status_note: Implemented with 5 classes (angry/happy/neutral/sad/surprise). Uses 456 of the 458 wav files (2 are 0 bytes). The Kaggle page gives no description, origin or labelling procedure. The 3 clips `S95_BIL_CO14_G3` in the neutral folder may be angry, and there may be other label errors (unverified).
language_note: Telugu (Kaggle dataset name and KuralHub). Whisper large-v3 language ID (all 456 clips, no human check): te 382, en 35, a few others; among the 333 clips with confidence >= 0.9, te 325 and en 8. Some utterances mix in English phrases (several of 12 transcribed clips, e.g. `I like you guys too`). English detections are frequent for surprise (16/85) and absent for angry (0/96).
license_note: Kaggle license field: Apache 2.0 (declared by the individual uploader, Jetty Sowmith). The page has no description, citation, origin or statement about speakers' consent; the recording's origin is unknown. Since it downloads from Kaggle with an Apache 2.0 license field, it stays `open` (maintainer, 2026-10-20).
release_version: Kaggle version 1 (Initial release), last updated 2024-05-16, one zip (210,266,003 bytes; 336,083,448 bytes extracted)
labels_discrete_note: Labels are folder names (angry 96, happy 94, neutral 103, sad 80, suprised 85; the folders are spelled `nuetral` and `suprised`). 2 sad files are 0 bytes, leaving 78 sad (456 in total). File names contain emotion codes (AN / HA / NU / SA / SU); checking all files, 100 of the 103 in the neutral folder are NU and 3 are SA (`S93_HAP_C11_G1_D03_SPKM03_V1_SA4_MMM`, `S95_BAB_CO8_G1_D02_SPKM03_V1_SA5_MMM`, `S95_BAB_CO8_G1_D04_SPKM03_V1_SA5_MMM`, all speaker SPKM03). The maintainer listened to these 3 and heard neutral, so the folder label (neutral) is kept. The other 4 folders match their codes. The labelling procedure and annotators are undocumented. Possible label errors: the 3 clips `S95_BIL_CO14_G3` in the neutral folder (`d01_v1`, `d01_v2`, `d03_v1`; speaker SPKM03) sounded angry to the maintainer (2026-10-20), and their median F0 (176-179 Hz) is closer to that speaker's angry (192-229 Hz) than neutral (133-139 Hz) (their loudness is lower, not matching angry). With no documentation this cannot be settled, so the label stays neutral as distributed (maintainer's decision). Only part was listened to, so other errors may exist.
label_basis_note: Only a third-party survey (KuralHub) calls it acted; the Kaggle description is empty. Nothing documents how labels were made.
lexical_confound_note: Nothing documents the scripts; not measured.
annotations_other: Speaker (`SPK[MF]nn` in the file name), file-name fields of unknown meaning
notes: KuralHub lists this data as Sowmith et al (2024), acted, 5 emotions (happy, sad, angry, neutral, surprised), 468 clips (paper unverified; KuralHub only points to the Kaggle page and has no description of its own). The release has 458 wav files, 2 of them 0 bytes. The Kaggle page's description, subtitle, tags and citation are all empty; recording procedure, speakers and labelling are unknown. File names have 10 fields such as `S45_SRI_C01_G1_D02_SPKF23_V1_SA5_MMM`; only the speaker (`SPK[MF]nn`, 20 people) and the emotion code are interpretable. 16-bit stereo, 447 at 44.1 kHz and 9 at 48 kHz (456 used). 0.26-27.22 s (mean 4.17 s), 0.5285 h in total. The two channels differ in all 456. No duplicates (md5 or decoded). arXiv 1006.4548 (HMM emotion recognition with TRDAP) was read, but no connection to this data could be confirmed. With no information on origin, procedure or speakers, its standing is unclear. Labels are the distributor's folder names and may contain errors (see labels_discrete_note); interpret results on this data with care.

name: TESS

sheet_notes: These stimuli were modeled on the Northwestern University Auditory Test No. 6 (NU-6; Tillman & Carhart, 1966). A set of 200 target words were spoken in the carrier phrase "Say the word _____' by two actresses (aged 26 and 64 years) and recordings were made of the set portraying each of seven emotions (anger, disgust, fear, happiness, pleasant surprise, sadness, and neutral). There are 2800 stimuli in total. Two actresses were recruited from the Toronto area. Both actresses speak English as their first language, are university educated, and have musical training. Audiometric testing indicated that both actresses have thresholds within the normal range. (2010-06-21)

status_note: Implemented with 4 classes (angry / happy / neutral / sad); uses 951 of the 952 clips. The card does not say where the audio comes from, and the source_prefix in the file names is the emotion initial, not a source id.

label_basis_note: The card calls them short naturalistic utterances, but the origin of the audio (source_prefix in the file names) is not explained. Each clip was labelled independently by 3 native speakers; majority vote with at least 2 agreeing; clips without a majority were excluded. Fleiss' kappa = 0.46. What the raters heard (audio only or not) is not stated.
lexical_confound_note: Naturalistic utterances of unstated origin, so the content is not controlled. Transcripts are distributed, so a check is possible but was not made.
notes: Hugging Face user OlhaHavryliuk, created 2026-04-30; no paper or citation on the card. 952 clips, 4 emotions (angry 259, happy 244, sad 227, neutral 222); speaker_id has 400 anonymous values; gender from the file-name suffix (593 female, 359 male). All 16 kHz mono 16-bit, 0.523-5.501 s, 0.5463 h. The card calls them short naturalistic utterances but gives no origin of the audio; in the file name {source_prefix}_{clip_id}_{gender}.wav the prefix is the emotion initial (a/h/s/n, matching the label in all 952), although the card calls it a source identifier. A Ukrainian transcript is given for every clip. Four speaker ids appear with both genders. The official split is speaker-disjoint (train 771 / test 181; 348 and 52 speakers); the card says speakers were assigned greedily to balance emotion and gender. Citation (Mendeley's Cite this dataset): Ali, Md Rayhan; Saeef, Sadman; Mohammad, Mohammad Miftahul Islam Irfan; Khan, Maliha; Hasan, Suchi; Das, Sajib; Aurpa, Tanjim Taharat; Hasan, Sharad (2026), "UFTBESD: University of Frontier Technology, Bangladesh-Bangla Emotional Speech Dataset", Mendeley Data, V4, doi: 10.17632/h3f8pjbw73.4

notes: 2026 (v4 fixed file-name inconsistencies and added a metadata CSV). 100 people aged 15-38 (50 male, 50 female) read 2 sentences once in each of 7 emotions. 44.1 kHz 16-bit wav, 0.74-6.04 s (mean 2.68 s). The release (v4) has 27 groups (68 wav files) with identical content (byte MD5 matches, as does the CRC in the zip). 21 groups put the same audio under different speakers (P_43/P_44/P_90, all 7 emotions of S1 and S2 = 14 groups; P_61/P_62, all 7 emotions of S2 = 7 groups). 6 groups put the same audio under two emotions of the same speaker and sentence (disgust/surprise for P_02, P_05, P_07, P_10, P_26; neutral/surprise for P_13). The maintainer listened to determine the correct labels, and the recipe excludes 41 files (leaving 1,359 files, 98 speakers). Measured total duration 1.041 h (1,400 files at the original 44.1 kHz). Metadata recording environment: indoor 1,288, outdoor 112; 40 device models. No paper is linked to the Mendeley record (2026-10-17, the articles field of the public API is empty).

name: USC-EMO-MRI
full_title: USC-EMO-MRI: An emotional speech production database
status_note: Audio is used after a dereverberation pre-processing step (see audio_format and notes in recipes). Implemented with 4 classes (neutral/angry/happy/sad). Labels are the majority vote of 10-12 listeners: the emotion listeners perceived, not the performers' intention. Emotion ID 5 (undocumented, 29 utterances) and utterances with no row in `meta` (29) are not used. Speaker-independent split.
license_note: Zenodo license field: CC BY 4.0 (deposited on Zenodo 2026-03-30). CC BY 4.0 requires attribution; the citation from Zenodo is used (as specified by the maintainer, 2026-10-19): Kim, J., Toutios, A., Kim, Y.-C., Zhu, Y., Lee, S., & Narayanan, S. (2014). USC-EMO-MRI: An emotional speech production database [Dataset]. 10th International Seminar on Speech Production (ISSP). USC-EMO-MRI corpus: An emotional speech production database recorded by real-time magnetic resonance imaging, Cologne, Germany. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19325044. The CSL paper (doi 10.1016/j.csl.2020.101100) is related but is not the citation for this corpus.
release_version: The single version of Zenodo 19325044 (created 2026-03-30, publication_date 2014-05-08). zip md5 65fa5b0cf0337a873227a490d56fdaf3
labels_discrete_note: `emotion ID` in `labels/meta` (README: the final label determined by listener evaluation). 1 neutral 656 / 2 angry 563 / 3 happy 542 / 4 sad 544 / 5: 29 (an ID the README does not explain; the paper's evaluation options include "other", but no source says 5 is other). 29 utterances have no row in `meta` and no label (the timing table has 2,363 rows, `meta` 2,334). The recipe uses the 2,305 utterances with IDs 1-4.
label_basis_note: 10 professional actors portrayed 4 target emotions. Each utterance was rated by at least 10 raters (professional actors) from the audio only: the best emotion of 5 choices (neutral, anger, happiness, sadness, other), confidence, and strength of expression (5 levels). The final label is the majority vote; ties go to the higher mean confidence. The recipe uses this final evaluation label (emotion ID in meta), not the target emotion.
lexical_confound_note: The same passage and sentences in every emotion.
annotations_other: Sentence ID, speaking rate, transcript, utterance times, speaker ID
notes: Kim, Toutios, Lee, Narayanan (USC SAIL). 5 men and 5 women with professional acting experience lay supine in an MRI scanner and read English sentences (6 sentences + repeated utterances for some speakers + the Grandfather passage) in 4 target emotions. The MRI captures the mid-sagittal plane of the vocal tract at 23.18 frames/s and 68x68 pixels; audio was recorded simultaneously at 20 kHz and denoised afterwards with adaptive signal processing (paper §2.2). Fast speaking rate only for neutral (98 utterances). The archive is AVI (video + audio); there are no wav files. Labels are the majority vote of the emotion perceived by 10-12 listeners (paper §2.3; listeners per speaker in Table 2); agreement with the target emotion ranges from 69.5% (M2) to 94.0% (F2) as speaker means. Per-rater choices, confidence and strength, and the performers' target emotions, are not in the archive (the paper's Data availability says "the emotion evaluation result of each utterance" is public). 26 AVI files (including 3 in `f3/avi/palate_sweep/`) do not appear in the timing table and are not explained in the README. Measured: 10 speakers, 356 AVI files, 2,363 utterances in the timing table, 2,334 with labels (2,305 with IDs 1-4). Speech acted inside an MRI scanner, not a corpus built for speech emotion recognition (the paper studies the articulation of emotional expression). The remaining noise level was not measured. Labels are the listeners' majority vote and some differ from the performers' intention. The recipe's valid set is a single speaker (f2). How to use it in multi-corpus training is undecided.

name: UTeMo
full_title: UTeMo audiovisual dataset for emotion recognition
status_note: Implemented with 7 classes (angry / disgust / fear / happy / neutral / sad / surprise); uses 1,780 of the 1,801 videos (audio extracted at 16 kHz): 21 videos with identical video and audio to another repetition of the same actor, emotion and phrase are left out, keeping the lowest repetition of each of 20 groups (maintainer's decision). Mendeley version 2 is used; its Utemo.zip is the same file as version 1.
license_note: Mendeley Data license field: CC BY NC 3.0 (re-read through the Mendeley API, 2026-10-26; checked by the maintainer). The README of version 2 adds that the dataset is intended strictly for research and academic purposes and asks to cite the Data in Brief paper (in revision).
release_version: Mendeley Data version 2 (2026-06-25); Utemo.zip is identical to version 1 (2024-02-20): same file id, size and SHA-256
label_basis_note: Label = the emotion in the file name (the state the actor portrayed). The README calls the samples validated but gives no procedure.
lexical_confound_note: Six phrases (F1-F6) are spoken in every emotion, but F7 is used only for neutral, sadness and surprise (106 clips) and F8-F10 only for neutral (78 clips, 31% of the neutral clips). So a few phrases reveal the label. The phrase texts are not in the release.
notes: UTeMo (Universidad Tecnologica de la Mixteca), Carrasco-Jimenez et al., Data in Brief 2026 (in revision). Audiovisual emotion database in Mexican Spanish: 14 actors (7 female, 7 male), 7 emotions, 1,801 videos (1920x1080, 30 fps; audio 48 kHz mono), about 105 min stated (the recipe's audio totals 2.0 h). File names <Emotion>_Actor<n>_P<m>_F<l>.avi (actor 1-14, repetition 1-3, phrase 1-10). Counts per emotion: sadness 289, surprise 279, neutral 254, anger 249, disgust 244, fear 244, happiness 242. Phrase texts are not in the release. Mendeley version 2 (2026-06-25) differs from version 1 (2024-02-20) only by the added README_Mendeley.md and a changed description ('first database' removed, 'balanced' became 'approximately balanced'); the Utemo.zip is byte-identical (verified by downloading it and comparing the SHA-256). 20 groups (41 files) have identical video and audio streams, each the same actor, emotion and phrase in another repetition; the recipe keeps the lowest repetition of each group and leaves out 21 files. Video is not used.

name: VoiceNet
full_title: VoiceNet: Fine-Grained Voice Understanding Beyond Emotion at Scale(VoiceNet-Emo / VoiceNet-Ext)
status_note: Evaluation data in which experts rated the presence of 40 emotions in real Emilia-Large audio (VoiceNet-Emo), plus ratings of 57 attributes (VoiceNet-Ext, provisional). Added at the request of the literature database (2026-10-23).
license_note: The paper says VoiceNet-Emo clips come from Emilia-YODAS (CC-BY-4.0) and Emilia (CC-BY-NC-4.0) and are released under CC-BY and CC-BY-NC research licenses; derivatives inherit the source clips' license. The repository code is MIT.
labels_discrete_note: VoiceNet-Emo: for each of 40 emotions (EmoNet-Voice taxonomy), whether the emotion is present, rated on 3 levels. Binary Fleiss' kappa between experts = 0.086. VoiceNet-Ext: 57 attributes, 40,990 ratings by 8 people over 18.5k pairs; kappa = -0.022 on the 5,583 items with 3 raters. The authors advise against using Ext scores for confirmatory ranking.
notes: LAION (Schuhmann, Kaczmarczyk et al., arXiv 2609.32016). Names in the repository: emolia-emo (= VoiceNet-Emo), emolia-dim (= VoiceNet-Ext). For training, the paper also releases Emolia-Balanced and data annotated with MOSS-Audio-8B-Thinking from LAION's Got Talent (1.69M clips), Majestrino (973k) and Multilingual In The Wild (721k) (VoiceNet organisation on Hugging Face). Majestrino and Multilingual In The Wild are speech corpora without emotion labels whose only emotion-related attributes are these automatic annotations, so they are not rows.

name: WHiSER
full_title: WHiSER: White House Tapes Speech Emotion Recognition Corpus
status_note: Implemented with 8 classes (angry / contempt / disgust / fear / happy / neutral / sad / surprise); uses 4,407 of the 5,427 clips. Left out: 47 labelled O (other) and 916 labelled X (no agreement), and 57 clips that repeat another clip (53 groups of identical or near-identical sound; of the 3 groups with conflicting labels all clips are dropped, otherwise the first by name is kept). The license is not stated and the authors are to be asked. The source is the Nixon tapes (1971-1973), distant microphones with reverberation and noise, so the domain is unusual; neutral is 78% of the used clips.
language_note: The paper does not state the language. Conversations in President Nixon's office (1971-1973)
license_note: The GitHub repository (msplabresearch/WHiSER, commit 5850655514dd, 2024-09-03) has no license file; the README and the paper state no terms of use. The audio is derived from recordings published by the Nixon Presidential Library. The maintainer will ask the authors (MSP lab) about license and citation (2026-10-26; not yet contacted); until then it is used locally only and not redistributed.
labels_discrete_note: Consensus is by plurality. X (no agreement) and O (other) also exist. Distributed labels: N 3,492, X 916, H 345, A 293, S 284, O 47, U 33, C 10, F 6, D 1
label_basis_note: Label = the plurality of at least five student workers' choices among eight primary emotions (A anger, C contempt, D disgust, F fear, H happy, N neutral, S sad, U surprise; O other and X no agreement are also coded). Individual annotations (with worker ids) and secondary emotions are in labels_detailed.csv. The 5,427 clips were first selected by emotion recognition models trained on MSP-Podcast (including a manual removal of unintelligible clips) so that they are likely to be emotional.
lexical_confound_note: Natural speech from the White House tapes judged by listeners who understood the words; the words may have influenced the labels. No transcripts are in the release.
annotations_other: Secondary emotions (16 kinds + Other), individual ratings per rater (labels_detailed), positions in the source recordings (Annotation_wav_files_ref.txt)
notes: Naini, Goncalves, Kohler, Robinson, Richerson and Busso (MSP lab, Interspeech 2024, pp. 1595-1599). Natural emotional speech from the Nixon White House tapes (1971-1973; Oval Office, Cabinet Room, telephone and other places) selected and annotated with the AndC pipeline: audio was converted to 16 kHz 16-bit mono, voice-activity segmented, filtered for music and noise (5 dB SNR floor), and emotionally likely turns were retrieved with models trained on MSP-Podcast; unintelligible ones were removed by hand. 5,427 clips of 3-11 s are annotated by 33 student workers, at least five per turn, with a primary emotion (8 options plus other), secondary emotions (16 kinds), and arousal, valence and dominance on a 7-point scale. The distributed wav files are 44.1 kHz (5,255) or 22.05 kHz (172) mono 32-bit float, 3.010-10.990 s, 6.3548 h (the paper says 16 kHz 16-bit and 6 h 21 min). Primary labels in labels_consensus.csv: N 3,492; X 916; H 345; A 293; S 284; O 47; U 33; C 10; F 6; D 1. SpkrID is Unknown and Split_Set NA for every file. The README lists Annotation_wav_files_ref.txt (mapping to the source recordings), which is not published. The paper says duplicates were removed, but 53 groups (107 clips) of the same sound remain, most of them the same tape under another name (e.g. rmn_e655a and rmn_e655b), 22 of them across the recipe's splits before exclusion.

Like Emolia (emilia_emotion) it is based on Emilia-YODAS audio, but whether it is a subset of Emolia was not checked.
